flow: Each unit of work is a forked swe-coder DAG on a feature branch -> pushes -> opens a PR into main referencing its issue -> overseer schedules a review DAG -> overseer gates/merges. CI via GitHub Actions; CD via ArgoCD on k3s. Bugs -> issues -> fix DAGs. Lockfile/rebase conflicts (a sibling landing restales an open PR's Cargo.lock) are cleared by a forked relock/rebase DAG, never inline (P1). (This PR-into-main flow follows the explicit user request and supersedes the app's local-first default.)

known_patterns.lockfile_restale_on_land: Every land to main moves the base and MAY restale the Cargo.lock of a still-open sibling PR that branched from an earlier commit — BUT ONLY IF the two sides' lockfile changes textually overlap. If the sibling PRs add package nodes in NON-overlapping regions (alphabetically distant [[package]] blocks), git text-merges them cleanly and there is NO conflict. First observed at I14: landing #16 (ferric-router #5) at I13 restaled PR #15 (ferric-http #6) -> I15 forked ferric-http-relock-r1. I16's chirp-types #7 land (squash 2e32aed) was EXPECTED to restale PR #15 again, but at I17 the live gh poll showed PR #15 OPEN/MERGEABLE/CLEAN: chirp-types ('c') and ferric-http ('f') added non-overlapping additive Cargo.lock nodes with zero version churn, so git merged them cleanly and NO relock-r2 was needed. LESSON: always CONFIRM restale via the live gh mergeability poll, never by assumption — a sibling land does not necessarily conflict. When a PR IS CONFLICTING, clear it with one forked relock/rebase DAG (check out work/<slug>, merge origin/main, regenerate Cargo.lock via cargo build, re-run the synthesis gate, push), never inline (P1).
known_patterns.gh_mergeability_async: gh pr view returns mergeable/mergeStateStatus=UNKNOWN on a fresh query; GitHub computes it asynchronously. Re-poll until it is not UNKNOWN before gating a land. Never land on UNKNOWN; never land CONFLICTING.
known_patterns.gh_self_review_block: gh pr review --approve is rejected (Can not approve your own pull request) because the authenticated gh account authored the PR; the fallback posts --comment (state COMMENTED). The authoritative APPROVE/REQUEST-CHANGES verdict is in the review DAG's SYNTHESIS.md body, not the gh review state.
